title: Multi-Syllable Stress Suffix Rules (-tion, -ic, -ty, -ee)
objectives: Predict stress placement in multi-syllable derivative words
Apply penultimate and antepenultimate stress rules
Maintain rhythmic accentuation in long words

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner stresses first syllable of "university".
💡 Solution: Count 3 syllables from the end: u-ni-VER-si-ty.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Multi-Syllable Stress Suffix Rules (-tion, -ic, -ty, -ee)
1. Definition: Multi-syllable words follow predictable stress placement rules based on their suffixes.

2. Rule: 1. -tion, -sion, -ic, -ical = Primary stress on syllable BEFORE suffix (information, fantastic). 2. -ty, -cy, -phy, -gy, -al = Primary stress 3rd syllable from end (university, democracy). 3. -ee, -eer, -ese = Primary stress ON suffix (guarantee, volunteer).
3. Why? English adopted Latin and Greek suffix stress rules during historical borrowing.
4. How to recognize? Identify suffix endings in words of 3 or more syllables.
5. Common examples: information /ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/, fantastic /fænˈtæstɪk/, university /ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːrsəti/, guarantee /ˌɡærənˈtiː/
6. Counter-examples: Germanic suffixes (-ness, -ful, -less) which do not change root stress.
7. Exceptions: arabic /ˈærəbɪk/ (stress on first syllable instead of before -ic).
8. Common mistakes: Stressing the wrong syllable in long academic words (*inFORmation instead of inforMAtion).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: -tion and -ic = Syllable right BEFORE! -ee = Right ON the suffix!
10. Key vocabulary: multi-syllable stress, suffix rule, penultimate, antepenultimate, rhythm
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟠 B1
13. Associated Visual: 📈 Peak highlight on the stress-designated syllable before the suffix.
14. Key Takeaway: -tion and -ic = Stress BEFORE suffix! -ee = Stress ON suffix!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Where is stress placed in words ending in -tion like "information"? (On the syllable immediately before -tion)
CCQ 2: Where is stress placed in words ending in -ee like "guarantee"? (Directly on the suffix -ee)
CCQ 3: Does adding -ness change the stress on "kind"? (No, Germanic suffixes do not move stress)

teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.
